key_insight: Controlling the variance of off-policy importance ratios stabilizes asynchronous, critic-free policy-gradient training for LLMs, allowing high-throughput asynchronous RL without a few stale samples dominating updates.
problem_solved: Asynchronous RL with critic-free policy gradients (e.g., REINFORCE, GRPO) suffers from very high gradient variance because stale rollouts produce heavy-tailed importance ratios, causing unstable updates and poor scalability.
method: Variance-controlled off-policy corrections: limit heavy tails in importance ratios via clipping, regularization, and adaptive reweighting to reduce estimator variance.
Staleness-aware data handling: schedule or reweight stale rollouts and manage replay buffers to prevent a small fraction of stale samples from dominating gradients.
Asynchronous protocol adjustments: integrate lightweight variance control into the async worker←→learner pipeline to preserve throughput while improving stability.
impact: Enables scalable, stable asynchronous RL for LLM fine-tuning (e.g., RLHF, reasoning tasks) by reducing catastrophic, high-variance updates—improving sample efficiency and end-to-end throughput in practical training systems.
visual_elements: System diagram: asynchronous workers generating rollouts -> central learner with a 'variance control' module (iconic pipeline).
Distribution chart: importance-ratio histogram before (heavy tail) vs after variance control (trimmed/regularized).
Line plot: training variance and performance vs asynchrony level showing improved stability and throughput.
Annotated flow: replay-buffer/staleness reweighting schematic highlighting sample weighting and clipping steps.
paper_title: Stable Asynchrony: Variance-Controlled Off-Policy RL for LLMs
paper_authors: Luke Huang, Zhuoyang Zhang, Qinghao Hu, Shang Yang, Song Han
